page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU ratio. The instance runs on an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes an L1d cache of 48 KB, an L2 cache of 2 MB, and an L3 cache of 260 MB. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance alongside weaker multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. The instance achieved average tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU performance (1564.68) and Geekbench single-core testing (1868.0). However, multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (4154.0) and stress-ng multi-core (3219.87), fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests also show lower-tier performance, with uncached large block reads at 33.17 GB/sec and writes at 21.19 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the n4-highmem-4 provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. It is suitable for small-scale database operations, caching layers, text processing, and basic web serving, where its 7.0 GB/sec static web serving throughput is sufficient. However, it is less suited for heavy multi-threaded compute tasks, software compilation, or complex image processing due to its lower multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmark ratings.
